To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a combination HS-RDT that is capable of identifying asymptomatic infections and that can differentiate Plasmodium species would be highly valued by end-users in malaria control programmes, and would be used to support malaria elimination efforts.
a new generation of highly sensitive rapid diagnostic test is needed to support active case detection for malaria elimination.

(i) ACD is a common activity in malaria elimination settings and (ii) a combination highly sensitive RDT that can detect all infected individuals and differentiate species, and that is portable, low-cost and easy to read, would be a valuable tool to support ACD in malaria elimination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new generation of RDTs to support the elimination of malaria.
the development of a next-generation combination highly sensitive rapid malaria diagnostic test to support active case detection strategies for malaria elimination.
the development of a new generation of RDTs, with improved sensitivity, to guide the development and implementation of ACD strategies for malaria elimination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination HS-RDT should detect Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax species, be low-cost, lightweight and portable and provide results that are immediately interpretable with the naked eye, to support malaria control and elimination programmes.
there is an important need for a next-generation RDT that could be adopted by malaria programmes to support ACD activities for radical cure.
a combination HS-RDT with Pf, Pv, and Pan detection is preferred for malaria elimination, with the possibility to replace existing tests for ACD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a combination HS-RDT that detects all Plasmodium spp. infections and differentiates Plasmodium species would be the most desirable for use in ACD and radical treatment activities in malaria endemic countries.

the survey results suggest that a next-generation combination highly sensitive RDT could be a useful tool to support ACD strategies for malaria elimination, and that it could be adopted by malaria control programme managers and end-users if the product characteristics are well aligned with the needs of their programmes.
the new combination HS-RDTS need to be simple, easy to interpret and able to detect asymptotic infections and differentiate species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is an urgent need for a new combination HS RDT to support ACT in ACD.
the diagnostic community should work with malaria programmes to develop new diagnostic tools that are fit-for-purpose and can be used to accelerate malaria elimination.

the current generation of RDTs is insufficient to support ACD activities in elimination settings and new combination HS-RDTS, able to detect all infected individuals and identify all species, are needed to achieve malaria elimination.
